public_signal: Bosch describes steer-by-wire as steering wheel actuator, steering rack actuator, software functions, no mechanical link, and redundant data/power supply.
what_it_supports: SbW has a common component architecture and supplier-owned system boundary.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not prove a buyer has unmet need for external assessment or that a target supplier lacks equivalent artifacts.
eps_supplier_use: Use as public architecture and redundancy reference.
decision: Keep as source, not value proof

public_signal: Bosch and Arnold NextG describe cooperation toward commercial-scale market launch of steer-by-wire.
what_it_supports: SbW is moving from research theme toward commercial implementation.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not prove paid support demand for EPS suppliers.
eps_supplier_use: Use only as market transition evidence.

public_signal: ZF describes by-wire chassis systems without mechanical connection or system fluids and expects a significant share of the steer-by-wire market by 2030.
what_it_supports: Supplier-side market movement and industrialization are public.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not show what documentation gaps remain inside target EPS suppliers.
eps_supplier_use: Use as market transition and supplier-positioning evidence.

public_signal: ZF says it will supply Mercedes-Benz steer-by-wire technology from 2026.
what_it_supports: There is public evidence of OEM adoption path and supplier role.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not prove a generic evidence-pack business.
eps_supplier_use: Use as proof that supplier/OEM interface exists in public market.

public_signal: Nexteer describes the hand-wheel side, wheel-side actuator, system software/integration, dual hardware, and multi-path processing software.
what_it_supports: Public supplier materials converge on hand-wheel side, wheel-side, software, and redundancy architecture.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not reveal target DTCs, freeze frame, security policy, or customer RFQ questions.
eps_supplier_use: Use as architecture and redundancy vocabulary source.
decision: Keep as source, not value proof

public_signal: Schaeffler positions the wheel-side steering unit as a steer-by-wire architecture element.
what_it_supports: The wheel-side steering unit can be treated as a public component boundary.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not show diagnostic or safety artifact gaps.
eps_supplier_use: Use for the one-case sample around partial loss of wheel-side redundancy.

public_signal: Schaeffler explains steer-by-wire experience, steering-column elimination, sensors, and feedback motor.
what_it_supports: SbW affects driver feedback and cockpit/mechanical architecture.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not prove EPS supplier paid workflow pain.
eps_supplier_use: Use as public explanation of HWA/feedback implications.

public_signal: HELLA describes steering torque and angle becoming electrical signals and a redundant steering sensor architecture.
what_it_supports: Sensor redundancy is a public supplier-owned subtopic.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not cover full SbW system diagnosis or business value.

source_name: JTEKT engineering journal redundant SbW system
public_signal: JTEKT describes parallel redundant system examples including CAN, power cables, motors, and ECUs.
what_it_supports: Redundant architecture is not new and has technical precedent.
what_it_does_not_support: It is older technical material and not proof of current buyer demand.
eps_supplier_use: Use as caution that redundancy explanation may already be standard.

public_signal: Tesla describes multiple redundant sensors/actuators, alert, chime, torque reduction, pull-over instruction, power cycle, and low-speed override.
what_it_supports: Driver-visible degraded behavior can be publicly observed as an owner-manual topic.
what_it_does_not_support: It is vehicle-specific and does not prove other OEM or supplier demand.
eps_supplier_use: Use as scenario seed for degraded redundancy one-page sample.

source_name: NHTSA generic steer-by-wire functional safety assessment
public_signal: NHTSA/Volpe report covers functional safety assessment, FMEA, safety requirements, safe states, and DTC coverage areas.
what_it_supports: SbW safety and diagnostic coverage are existing public safety-analysis topics.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not support selling generic safety analysis as new value.
eps_supplier_use: Use as baseline that weakens generic evidence-pack positioning.
decision: Kill signal for generic safety offer

source_name: UK VCA R79 steer-by-wire compliance article
public_signal: VCA explains R79 Annex 6 requires documentation, fault strategy, verification, and may use FMEA/FTA or similar safety process.
what_it_supports: Documentation and verification are already expected in approval context.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not prove unmet supplier workflow demand.
eps_supplier_use: Use as evidence that certification/safety artifact packaging is not novel.
decision: Kill signal for generic certification offer

public_signal: R79 provides the steering-equipment regulation baseline including complex electronic vehicle control system documentation expectations.
what_it_supports: SbW must be discussed against existing steering regulation baseline.
what_it_does_not_support: It does not show business pain or target system gaps.
eps_supplier_use: Use as regulatory baseline, not sales proof.
